educationalGoal: In Japanese Communication 3, students aim for further development of basic grammar through communication tasks. Students will focus on developing skills of communication in modern Japanese reading, writing, speaking, and listening.
advice: Students will learn to conduct daily conversations in Japanese and deal with basic daily situations by focusing on fluency of basic grammar. Social and cultural manners and gestures necessary for appropriate communication with native speakers will also be introduced and reinforced with practical communication activities. This course has a Moodle course site. All important information about course related matters will be posted on this site. It is students' responsibility to check the site regularly.
books: Genki 1: An integrated course in elementary Japanese, third edition [The Japan Times Publishing] Genki 2: An integrated course in elementary Japanese, third edition [The Japan Times Publishing]
requiredKnowledge: Students must have completed Genki I grammar or possess equivalent knowledge or Japanese 100 level with a grade of C or higher.

activityGoals.body: Conduct short conversations based on daily situations.
Understand social and cultural manners in order to have appropriate communication.
Pick up important information from authentic materials.
Distinguish the difference between the written language and spoken language.

小テスト ① レ Daily review quizzes will assess students' understanding of grammar structures, kanji, vocabulary, and culturally appropriate usage. Quizzes are usually given at the beginning of class.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤     ⑥     レポート ① レ Students will take turns presenting a kanji they have found in real-life contexts, such as signs, menus, or instructions. This activity helps build practical kanji knowledge and encourages students to engage with the language in their daily environment. Kanji introduced may be included in review quizzes.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     成果発表
(口頭・実技) ① レ Students will give a short in-class speech (approximately 1 minute). The speech should be based on a personal experience, such as a recent event, cultural observation, travel experience, or daily life in Japan. This activity is designed to improve spoken fluency, build confidence, and encourage cultural exchange. Students are expected to prepare in advance and speak without reading a full script.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤     ⑥     作品 ①      ②     ③     ④     ⑤     ⑥     ポートフォリオ ① レ Students are required to complete a project of their own choosing. They must make three reports to the instructor. The first report will be the project proposal, and students must have the instructor’s permission to start. The mid-term report must be submitted.
